did_you_know.text: Did you know? After completing the work on the temple, Solomon placed in the treasuries of the house of God the sacred objects, the silver, the gold, and all the vessels that his father David had dedicated.

Did you know? Solomon assembled in Jerusalem the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, and the chiefs of the fathers’ houses to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, which is Zion.
Did you know? The people gathered before the king during the festival in the seventh month; thus, bringing up the ark became a national and festive event for all Israel.
Did you know? Along with the ark of the covenant, the priests and Levites also brought up the Tent of Meeting and all the holy furnishings that were in it.
Did you know? The ark of the covenant was brought into the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, and placed beneath the wings of the cherubim.

Did you know? The poles of the ark were so long that their ends could be seen from the front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside it; according to the text, they remained there during his lifetime.

Did you know? The text emphasizes that the ark contained only the two tablets of the covenant that Moses had placed there at Horeb, as part of the covenant the Lord made with Israel when they came out of Egypt.
Did you know? All the priests who had consecrated themselves took part in the service together, without being divided into shifts, when the ark was brought into the temple.

Did you know? The Levite musicians—including Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun—stood east of the altar, dressed in fine linen and playing cymbals, harps, and lyres; alongside them, 120 priests blew trumpets.

Did you know? When the trumpeters and singers raised their voices as one in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord, the temple was filled with a cloud, and the priests could not stand and minister because the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
